name: Jarvis
description: Voice-first browser assistant with an indexed fact store. Hold to talk, replies read back, facts remembered between sessions. Bring-your-own-key prototype; the conversation goes to Anthropic.
author: USER

data_streams.purpose: What the user told the assistant to remember, with aliases and an inverted index over both
data_streams.retention: until the user clears the browser origin's storage — there is no server copy to clear
data_streams.description: IndexedDB in the user's browser. Corrections are written beside the record rather than over it, so a superseded fact stays readable as superseded. Absence is a stored value: 'no answer was given' and 'nothing was asked' are different rows.

data_streams.purpose: Scheduled prompts the user asked for
data_streams.description: On the web these are in-page timers, so a closed tab fires nothing. Reported as durable: false in the capability panel rather than silently downgraded. The Capacitor wrap is the fix and has never been compiled — see notes.android.

data_streams.purpose: The turn being answered, plus the facts retrieval selected for it
data_streams.retention: session in the page; unknown at the provider
data_streams.description: SENT OFF DEVICE. Every turn goes to api.anthropic.com with the user's own API key. Retrieval decides which stored facts are attached, so what leaves varies by question and is not bounded by a fixed field list.

data_streams.retention: until cleared in the app or by clearing site data
data_streams.description: localStorage, which is readable by any script on the page. The capability ladder reports this rung by name rather than calling it secure storage; the Capacitor build can reach a better rung and has not been run.

data_streams.purpose: An optional connection to a willow-mcp orchestrator instance the user points this app at
data_streams.retention: until disconnected in settings or cleared by clearing site data
data_streams.description: The willow-mcp base URL, the dynamically-registered OAuth client_id, and the discovered authorize/token endpoints are non-secret and sit in localStorage. The OAuth access and refresh tokens go through the same key-storage rung the Anthropic key uses (app-private preferences natively, localStorage on the web). Nothing here is present until the user opens settings and signs in; see notes.willow.

network: outbound: api.anthropic.com (model inference), the browser's own speech-recognition service — see notes.speech — and, only if the user configures one in settings, a willow-mcp instance's HTTP+OAuth serve endpoint at a URL the user supplies — see notes.willow

notes.status: Prototype, re-landed from the quick-stupids playground. It runs and it is gated; it has not been used by anyone but its author.
notes.not_client_only: The other browser-side apps in this store declare client_only and mean it. This one cannot. Every conversational turn is sent to a third-party API, the key sits in localStorage, and speech recognition is not on-device. Declared as mixed so the catalog does not overstate it.
notes.local_processing: 0.0 is a deliberate understatement, and the field is a poor instrument for this app. What IS local: the fact store, the inverted index, ranking, alias expansion, reminder scheduling, and every capability probe. What is NOT: inference and speech-to-text, which is to say every turn the user can see. Rating it 0.9 because most of the CODE runs locally would describe the repository rather than the exposure. A number that has to be explained in prose is not doing the work of a number, and inventing precision here is the failure this store's own apps have elsewhere at 0.96.
notes.speech: Chrome and Safari implement SpeechRecognition against a SERVER-SIDE recognition service, so holding to talk sends audio off the device to the browser vendor as well as sending the transcript to Anthropic. This is documented engine behaviour rather than something measured here — provenance: assumed — and jarvis's own README did not mention it before this re-land. Firefox has no SpeechRecognition at all, so on Firefox there is no speech egress and no speech input.
notes.store_scope: Deliberately absent. field-acoustics and marching-arts declare a store_scope because they read and write the shared SOIL store. This app touches neither SOIL nor the vault — its storage is browser IndexedDB and localStorage, on the user's own machine. Declaring an empty or unused scope would be a claim about a surface that does not exist.
notes.android: apps/jarvis/android/ is a real Capacitor project and has NEVER BEEN COMPILED. No APK exists. The bridge is checked statically against the installed plugin definitions — 37 checks — which proves the symbols exist and proves nothing about the device. Committed rather than dropped, because dropping it would hide the gap instead of closing it.
notes.ci_blind_spots: This is the first app in the store with no Python in it, and every store-floor scanner globs *.py. The four drift-guard suites therefore skip it. tools/vault_leak_lint.py did something worse: it enumerated the app, opened none of its files, found no findings, and printed PASS jarvis (no local persistence) -- a green line whose second half is flatly false, since this app persists facts, reminders and an API key. That now reports UNKNOWN instead, with tests/test_vault_lint_vacuous_scan.py holding it. The floor still reads no line of this app's JavaScript; the difference is that it no longer claims to have.
notes.willow: src/willow.js is an OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + dynamic-client-registration client for willow-mcp's --serve mode, plus a minimal MCP JSON-RPC caller over its streamable-http transport. It is unconfigured and inert until the user enters a willow-mcp URL in settings and signs in. What is measured: the PKCE generation, the authorize-URL construction, and the SSE/JSON-RPC framing, by the suite. What is assumed, not measured: the discovered or guessed endpoint paths, the popup OAuth round trip, and token refresh — none of this has run against a live willow-mcp instance from this environment, which has no Google/Apple credentials and no willow-mcp process to test against. willow-mcp's own docs/design/human-orchestrator.md establishes that a signed-in, operator-bound session is gated entirely server-side (identity comes from the OAuth binding, never from anything this app asserts), so a bug in this client can misbehave or fail loudly but cannot grant itself standing it was not bound to.
